ai.description: The Greater Black Krait reaches 1.2–1.5m. It is uniformly glossy black or dark brown dorsally with a white venter. It lacks dorsal crossbands and possesses a distinctively triangular body cross-section.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bungarus niger* is uniquely distinguished by its uniform, glossy black dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct white crossbands or vertebral ridge scales seen in other kraits.
ai.habitat: *Bungarus niger* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often near streams, across the Himalayan foothills and Northeast India up to 1,500 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Greater Black Krait is primarily nocturnal and terrestrial, often emerging after dark to actively hunt for other snakes, lizards, and small mammals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bungarus niger* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–14 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing between August and October.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bungarus niger* occurs in the Himalayan foothills of Northeast India, Nepal, and Bhutan, typically ranging from the plains up to elevations of approximately 1,500 meters.
